Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator: Good afternoon. My name is Sarah, and I will be your conference operator today. After the speakers' remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session. Thank you. I will now turn the call over to Toshiya Hari.

Toshiya Hari: Thank you. Joining me today are Jensen Huang and Colette Kress. Our call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to significant risks and uncertainties, and our actual results may differ materially.

Colette Kress: Thanks, Toshiya. Revenue of $96.2 billion was a record, up 18% sequentially and up 106% year on year, driven by strong demand for Blackwell Ultra across hyperscalers and sovereign AI customers. NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA -1.52% ) continued to ramp.

Colette Kress: Data center compute revenue grew 21% sequentially. Networking revenue was a record as customers expanded scale-out and scale-up fabrics. Gross margin was 75.0%, and we expect gross margin to be in the mid-70s for the rest of the year as supply constraints ease.

Colette Kress: Turning to the outlook for the third quarter. Total revenue is expected to be $110 billion, plus or minus 2%. The magnitude of the memory price increase has exceeded our prior expectations, and we have factored that into our guidance.

Jensen Huang: Thank you, Colette. Demand for accelerated computing continues to grow as reasoning models and agentic AI drive a step change in compute. We see a multi-year build-out of AI factories around the world, and our supply chain partners are expanding capacity to meet it.

Jensen Huang: Export regulations continue to limit our ability to serve customers in China. We remain in active dialogue with the government and are not assuming any China data center revenue in our outlook.

Colette Kress: Gaming revenue was $4.9 billion, up 14% sequentially, as channel inventory normalized ahead of the holiday season. Professional visualization and automotive both grew double digits year on year on new design wins.

Colette Kress: We returned $15 billion to shareholders in the quarter through share repurchases and dividends. Operating expenses are expected to grow in the high-30s percent range for the full year as we invest in the next wave of AI infrastructure.

Jensen Huang: In closing, our Rubin platform is on track for production next year. The world is racing to build AI infrastructure and we are positioned to capture that opportunity with our full-stack platform. Thank you.

Operator: We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Your first question comes from the line of Vivek Arya with Bank of America. Your line is open.

Vivek Arya: Thanks for taking my question. Jensen, how should we think about the sustainability of demand into next year, given concerns about customer capex and power constraints?

Jensen Huang: Great question. The demand signals we see are stronger than ever. Customers are constrained by power and supply, not by appetite, and we expect growth to continue next year as new capacity comes online.

Operator: Your next question comes from Joe Moore with Morgan Stanley.

Joe Moore: Colette, could you talk about gross margin puts and takes as memory pricing rises and the product mix shifts toward rack-scale systems?

Colette Kress: Memory pricing is a headwind that we expect to largely offset through mix and cost improvements. We still expect gross margin in the mid-70s for the full year.
